This is a textbook example of a medium-size double-lobed radio galaxy. Two large radio lobes straddle an elliptical galaxy visible in red near the centre just below the optical PV diagram. So-called 'double' radio sources are a very common AGN morphology, and are made by supermassive black holes in the centres of massive elliptical galaxies. Their lobes can grow to enormous scales - sometimes much larger than the Milky Way. In fact, the lobes shown here are roughly 1 million lightyears across!
